newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin worries over its control of Russia regions.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin worries over its control of Russia regions.

text.p: Russia showed signs on Tuesday it wants to tighten up control of its 89 independence-minded regions.
President Boris Yeltsin wants to discuss the Kremlin's relations with the regions with regional leaders,Interfax news agency said.

Yeltsin made the request during a telephone conversation with Kremlin chief of staff Anatoly Chubais on Tuesday morning before he attended a meeting discussing Moscow's relations with the regions, the agency added.
Chubais told the meeting he was concerned by signs of weakening central control over the regions.
"After talking (with Yeltsin) on the telephone, Chubais urged all people at the meeting to prepare the necessary documents for talks with the president," Interfax said.
Chubais did not make clear whether Yeltsin planned to meet the regional chiefs or a small group of them, or whether he would make his message clear to them by other means.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said on Monday doctors had started a series of final tests to prepare the Kremlin leader for heart surgery and ordered him to cancel all his meetings this week.
Chubais made clear that the Kremlin was concerned by some recent decisions by regional leaders which, in Moscow's opinion, violated the constitution.
"These (decisions) are a result of the weakness of Russian state power," Interfax quoted Chubais as saying.
Chubais did not say what decisions he had in mind but made clear that the Kremlin would firmly stamp out any challenge to its leading role.
Moscow sent troops to Chechnya in December 1994 to try to crush its independence moves. Other regions have watched the fighting carefully but avoided open conflict with Moscow.

Some political analysts say a series of regional elections being held before the end of this year will replace local chiefs appointed by Moscow with elected leaders and make the Russian regions less dependent on the Kremlin's will.
In the first sign of their growing independence, some regional leaders have openly objected to a Kremlin campaign to boost budget revenues by clamping down on tax-dodging companies.
The president of the oil-rich ethnic republic of Tatarstan, Mintimer Shaimiyev, has said he will not accept any action launched against companies in Tatarstan without his approval.
Chubais said the Kremlin would seek to cancel all decisions made by local governors and councils which do not coincide with its policies.
"There will be a tough talks about this with the heads of local administrations," he said, adding that some of them might not be pleased with Moscow's planned moves.
